q: Ortho lab X-ray – diagnosis?
a:
Midshaft clavicle fracture – Allman group I

Description

  • AP view
  • Fracture of the middle 1/3 of the clavicle (most frequent)
  • Allman classification by location: I = midshaft · II = lateral · III = medial

Complications

  • Early: vascular & brachial plexus injury
  • Late: mal-union, non-union, callus formation (excessive bone)

Treatment

  • ORIF (screws & plates) if: neurovascular injury, open fracture, floating shoulder, ≥ 2 cm shortening

q: Ortho lab X-ray – diagnosis?
a:
Acromioclavicular dislocation – Rockwood type 5

Description

  • AP view
  • Severe superior displacement – clavicle very high
  • Major soft-tissue disruption
  • Rockwood: 1 = AC sprain (no displacement) · 2 = AC lig. tear, mild elevation (<25%) · 3 = AC + CC rupture, clavicle superior (piano-key sign) · 4 = distal clavicle posterior · 5 = severe superior displacement, major soft-tissue disruption · 6 = inferior, under acromion/coracoid

Complications

  • Instability, stiffness
  • Step (stair) deformity
  • K-wire migration if not removed (~3 months)

Treatment

  • Conservative (types 1, 2, sometimes 3): ice, rest, sling 3 weeks + early range-of-motion exercises
  • Surgical (higher types): ORIF / ligament reconstruction – K-wires, hook plate, screws, tight ropes

q: Ortho lab X-ray – diagnosis?
a:
Anterior shoulder dislocation

Description

  • Left: normal
  • Humeral head antero-inferior to the glenoid
  • Bankart lesion: antero-inferior glenoid rim fracture ± labrum tear
  • Hill-Sachs defect: postero-lateral humeral head compression fracture
  • Greater tuberosity fracture is most commonly associated

Complications

  • Axillary nerve damage
  • Associated fractures, Hill-Sachs defect
  • Irreducibility
  • Instability, recurrence, stiffness, arthrosis

Treatment

  • Non-surgical closed reduction:
  • – Kocher: external rotation, adduction, internal rotation
  • – Hippocrates: foot in the armpit + traction on the hand
  • – Milch-Moles: one doctor tracts axilla with a scarf, the other counter-tracts the hand
  • – Von Arlt: over the back of a chair
  • Sling & bandages for 3 weeks
